blocks.text: Documents the deliberate scope (health/quota/usage-history only) and explains why /api/capabilities isn't here. _LATENCY_PROBE_SAMPLES=5 is set at module level and explained in context: enough to see outliers without making the endpoint itself slow.
blocks.title: Module header and latency probe constant

blocks.text: _redact_host uses urlparse().hostname to strip credentials from connection URLs safely. _timed_calls runs a callable N times, measuring each with perf_counter(), and returns a summary dict. _postgres_ping executes SELECT 1 on a trusted cursor.
blocks.title: Private helpers: host redaction, timed-call loop, Postgres ping

blocks.text: health() is an unauthenticated check that simply returns {status: ok}. backend_latency_probe() runs timed pings against both Postgres and Redis, returning host names (redacted) and latency stats to let an operator compare the two backends' round-trip cost.
blocks.title: Health and latency endpoints

blocks.text: Seven stat-snapshot routes, one per module: chat page cache, DB pool, agent task pool, SGA, Laya routing gates, tool budget, and conversation threading. All follow the same pattern: require_auth, call a module-level get_*_stats() function, return whatever it returns. Comments explain the specific counter that motivated each endpoint.
blocks.title: In-process stats endpoints

blocks.text: quota() merges the daily quota snapshot with a live rate-window snapshot. usage_history() defaults to get_usage_history(days) but switches to get_usage_history_scoped when domain or workspace_id is provided, changing the response shape from {providers, accounts} to {dates, domain, workspace}.
blocks.title: Quota and usage history

gotchas: /api/capabilities is intentionally excluded from this file because it shares CAPABILITIES_MANIFEST with the not-yet-split notebooks routes
Sequential timing in _timed_calls is deliberate — it measures per-call latency, not throughput
stats routes require auth but do not scope to the caller — they expose aggregate server-wide counters
how_it_works: Every route except /api/health requires require_auth; all stats routes return aggregate counters with no per-user scoping beyond that
backend_latency_probe runs _postgres_ping and bus.ping each _LATENCY_PROBE_SAMPLES times sequentially and returns avg/min/max/samples
_redact_host strips credentials and path from connection URLs before returning them in API responses
usage_history branches on domain/workspace_id query params to call get_usage_history_scoped instead of get_usage_history
inputs: days, domain, workspace_id query params for usage_history
outputs: health status, latency numbers with host identifiers, stats dicts from each in-process module, quota snapshot, usage history
purpose: Groups the low-risk, no-shared-state operational endpoints that were the first batch split out of api/server.py. Covers health, per-backend latency measurement, hit/miss counters for every major in-process cache or pool, quota snapshot, and day-by-day usage history. No write operations.
summary: FastAPI router for health check, backend latency probe, in-process stats snapshots, quota, and usage history.

params.desc: a connection string such as a Postgres DSN or Redis REST URL, or None
params.name: raw_url

symbols.returns: hostname string (e.g. 'db.xyz.supabase.co') or None if input is None/empty
symbols.summary: Extracts only the hostname from a connection URL/DSN, discarding credentials, path, and query string.

params.desc: number of successive calls to make
params.name: samples

symbols.returns: dict with avg_ms, min_ms, max_ms (each rounded to 2dp) and samples_ms list
symbols.summary: Calls fn() 'samples' times sequentially, measures each call with perf_counter, and returns avg/min/max/samples_ms.
Executes SELECT 1 against Postgres using a trusted cursor to measure round-trip latency.
Unauthenticated liveness check that always returns {status: ok}.

symbols.returns: dict with postgres and redis keys, each containing host and latency_ms sub-dict
symbols.summary: Measures round-trip latency to both Postgres and Redis with 5 sequential pings each; returns host and stats for each.
Returns aggregate hit/miss counters for the Redis-backed chat page cache.
Returns aggregate checkout-outcome counters for the Postgres connection pool.
Returns counters tracking how often agent tasks started immediately vs queued on the dedicated agent-task executor.
Returns SGA resolve/escalate counters and breakdown of escalation reasons.

symbols.returns: dict with panel_gate and gatekeeper_gate keys, each containing mode, threshold, and stats
symbols.summary: Returns current mode/threshold and decision counters for both the panel gate and gatekeeper gate.
Returns increment and threshold-hit counters for the per-role-step tool call budget.
Returns counters tracking how often user-turn routing created new threads vs reused existing ones.
Returns wait/reroute/provider-failure counters recorded each time the LLM client makes a ledger-gating decision.

symbols.returns: merged dict from get_quota_snapshot() plus rate_windows key from get_rate_window_snapshot()
symbols.summary: Returns the daily quota snapshot merged with live minute/daily rate-window headroom for each provider key.

params.desc: number of calendar days to look back (1-90, default 7)
params.name: days

params.desc: optional domain filter; triggers scoped response shape
params.name: domain

params.desc: optional workspace filter; triggers scoped response shape
params.name: workspace_id

symbols.returns: {dates, providers, accounts} normally; {dates, domain, workspace} when domain or workspace_id is provided
symbols.summary: Returns day-by-day LLM usage for the last N days; switches to domain/workspace-scoped shape when filters are given.
